text:
The Commissioner of Police in the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Ahmed Sanusi, has directed Area Commanders and Divisional Police Officers (DPOs) to intensify patrols, surveillance and raids on identified criminal black spots ahead of the 2027 general elections.
Sanusi gave the directive during a meeting with senior officers of the command to strengthen security operations and ensure adequate preparedness for the forthcoming elections and end-of-year celebrations.
The directive was contained in a statement made available in Abuja by the FCT Police Command’s Public Relations Officer, SP Josephine Adeh.
The commissioner urged the officers to strengthen intelligence gathering and adopt proactive policing strategies to prevent criminal activities, particularly armed robbery, kidnapping, car theft and other violent crimes.
He also directed them to ensure strict compliance with electoral security guidelines to guarantee a peaceful, safe and orderly electoral process.
“As we approach the ember months and election period, I urge you to intensify patrols, surveillance and intelligence gathering.
“The idea is to prevent criminal activities, particularly armed robbery, kidnapping, car theft and other violent crimes,” he said.
Sanusi charged the officers to maintain professionalism, discipline and respect for human rights in the discharge of their duties, while ensuring prompt responses to distress calls from residents.
He further urged them to remain vigilant and proactive in identifying and addressing emerging security threats across the territory.
The CP also expressed concern over the increasing road construction activities within the city centre and their potential impact on traffic flow.
He directed the command’s traffic control departments and divisional traffic officers to strengthen traffic management and coordinate vehicular movements to reduce congestion and prevent obstructions on major roads.
Sanusi urged personnel deployed for traffic control to remain courteous and professional while ensuring the free flow of vehicles, particularly during peak periods.
He called on residents to remain security-conscious and promptly report suspicious movements and activities to the nearest police station or through the command’s emergency lines.
